# DOX — docs/ — Operator & Fleet Documentation

## Purpose

Per-audience documentation split. The root `llms.txt` stays the DOX rail
(agents read it top-down); this folder carries the human/operational
layers that were previously interleaved:

- `FLEET.md` — fleet state, machine inventory, hub addresses, per-machine
  setup receipts (windows host portproxy, mac shim state, router lanes).
- `OPERATIONS.md` — runbooks: bring-up, federation repair, envelope
  transfer, shim hardening, log hygiene, chat-integration contract.
- `ROADMAP.md` — refinement items (R1 identity persistence, R2 ledger,
  R3 operator-directed) and open defects with file/line anchors.

## Ownership

- Operator-facing summaries live here, NOT in the root `llms.txt`
  (which stays a lean contract for agents).
- AGENTS.md keeps the mission/security/worktree contract and points here
  for state; it does not duplicate fleet status.

## Local Contracts

- Fleet facts (versions, IPs, hub ids) must carry the date they were
  verified. Stale entries get updated or deleted on the next verified pass.
- Every doc file here ends with a `Verified:` line bearing the last check.

## Work Guidance

- When fleet state changes (hub version, router state, new machine), update
  `FLEET.md` in the same task and bump its `Verified:` line.
- New runbooks go in `OPERATIONS.md` only if they will recur; one-off
  procedures stay in `.agents/tasks/` records.

## Verification

- `grep -c 'Verified:' docs/*.md` — every doc carries one.
- Cross-check versions against `curl healthz` on both hubs during any
  fleet-touching task.

## Child DOX Index

(none — flat folder)
